findings.detail: PIK-marked floating-rate debt was classified as fixed despite an explicit SOFR-plus spread; retain basis_spread and classify the coupon as floating.

rationale: X04 is a Class 2 within-row issue. Raw SOI rows explicitly place S + in the Reference Rate & Spread field next to the reported spreads, including the cited 7.00% and 8.00% PIK examples. Thus basis_spread is source-supported; the conflicting fixed_coupon classification is wrong, most likely because the PIK label obscured the floating-rate structure. No aggregate anchor is applicable. Residual risk is limited to uncited members of the ten-row issue group, but the repeated source layout and cited rate patterns establish the common mechanism.
